page.h1: Best laptop screen extender for a 15.6-inch laptop
page.desc: Which laptop screen extenders match a 15.6-inch laptop in height and sharpness, what each one needs from your laptop's ports, and where to buy each at its maker's price on 2026-11-21.
page.answer: Short answer. The best laptop screen extender for a 15.6 inch laptop has 15.6-inch 1080p panels, which match its screen at 7.65 in tall and 141 PPI: the Aura Dual Go Max 15.6 adds two, no driver, if your laptop has two video outputs. A 14.1-inch screen draws everything 9.6% smaller.

page.after:
What the differences mean

All the figures below assume your laptop has the usual 15.6-inch 16:9 screen at 1920×1080. A 16:10 or QHD laptop screen changes the match. Each figure is worked out from the screen size and resolution the maker states.

  • Your laptop's screen: 15.6 × 16 ÷ 18.358 = 13.60 in wide; 15.6 × 9 ÷ 18.358 = 7.65 in tall; √(1920² + 1080²) ÷ 15.6 = 2202.9 ÷ 15.6 = 141.2 PPI.
  • 15.6-inch 1080p extender (both Aura models, UPERFECT): the same sum gives 7.65 in and 141.2 PPI, so a 0.00 in height difference. Text and windows are the same physical size on all three screens.
  • Trio 3 Pro, 14.1-inch 16:10 at 2240×1400: 14.1 × 10 ÷ 18.868 = 7.47 in tall (0.18 in shorter); √(2240² + 1400²) ÷ 14.1 = 2641.5 ÷ 14.1 = 187.3 PPI, so it is sharper but draws text smaller unless you raise its scaling.
  • Duex Float 2 Pro, 16-inch 16:10 at 2560×1600: 16 × 16 ÷ 18.868 = 13.57 in wide (0.03 in narrower). It sits directly above the laptop, so width is the edge that lines up. 16 × 10 ÷ 18.868 = 8.48 in tall; 3018.9 ÷ 16 = 188.7 PPI.
  • A 14.1-inch 1080p screen: 14.1 × 9 ÷ 18.358 = 6.91 in tall (0.74 in shorter); 2202.9 ÷ 14.1 = 156.2 PPI; 141.2 ÷ 156.2 = 0.904, so everything draws 9.6% smaller.
  • Price per added screen at the makers' stores, 2026-11-21: Dual Go Max $329.00 ÷ 2 = $164.50; UPERFECT BE156MF $379.99 ÷ 2 = $190.00; Dual Boost Pro Max Slim $409.00 ÷ 2 = $204.50. These are Black Friday prices.

The pick is a screen we do not link: Aura's Dual Go Max 15.6. Of the two-screen sets in stock on 2026-11-21, it is the lowest-priced one whose panels match a 15.6-inch 1080p laptop and that needs no software. Among the screens we link, the Duex Float 2 Pro wins the one-added-screen case: Mobile Pixels rates it for 15–16-inch laptops, it matches your screen's width, and it runs from one cable. The Trio 3 Pro wins the clip-on two-screen case. Mobile Pixels' prices change with timed sales: the Trio 3 Pro was {price:mobile-pixels-trio-3-pro} on its store on 2026-11-21. Dealectric does not test units. The figures here come from makers and the reviewers named.

Why panel size and sharpness decide a 15.6-inch match

An extender with the same diagonal, shape and resolution as your laptop screen has the same pixels per inch. A window or a spreadsheet row is then the same physical size on every screen, and the screens' edges line up. That is why the 15.6-inch 1080p sets lead this table. A sharper 14.1-inch or 16-inch panel (187–189 PPI) shows more detail, but it draws text smaller until you raise that screen's scaling. A 14.1-inch 1080p screen draws everything 9.6% smaller and stands 0.74 in shorter than the laptop beside it.

The second check is whether the screens run on your laptop at all, and the makers' own wording settles it. Screens that need no software need one video output per added screen. Aura says the Dual Go Max needs "two video outputs". FOPO says its S10 needs either two video-capable USB-C ports or "USB-C + HDMI + USB-A power". Running two screens from one cable means installing a driver: Aura says "One quick driver install on first use" for the Dual Boost Pro Max Slim. Makers also count screens differently. Mobile Pixels' "Dual Screen" Duex adds one screen and its "Tri-Screen" Trio adds two, while Aura's "Dual" adds two. FOPO states that "Base M1, M2 and M3 MacBooks are not supported" for the S10's two-screen setup. A base M1, M2 or M3 MacBook is better served by one added screen.

Measurements also show that power matters. Notebookcheck measured the dual 15.6-inch UPERFECT Delta at 226 cd/m² on its adapter and 160 cd/m² on one USB-C cable. Macworld found the Duex Float 2 Pro capped at 80% brightness on 7.5 W laptop power and recommends a 15 W or larger charger. Macworld also says the Trio 3 Pro cannot reach full brightness on laptop power alone. Budget a wall charger for any of these.

What was left out, and why. The table keeps to screens whose maker states a laptop range that includes 15.6 inches, plus freestanding screens, which have no lid to fit. FOPO's S10 has two 15.6-inch 1080p panels, a 12.0–17.3-inch laptop range (FOPO's) and needs no driver. It would match as well as the Aura pair, but FOPO's store showed it sold out on 2026-11-21. The Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS is a 14.1-inch 1080p screen and the mismatch shown above. Its maker's laptop range could not be read on 2026-11-21. Mobile Pixels' Fold 15.6-inch (1080p) was $143.99 at its store on 2026-11-21, but its port and power details could not be read, so it is not in the table. The ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK is a freestanding 15.6-inch 1080p screen with two DisplayPort Alt Mode USB-C ports and mini HDMI (ASUS). ServeTheHome measured 140.2 nits and ITPro measured 205 cd/m², against ASUS's 250 cd/m² rating. ASUS's US store showed no price for it on 2026-11-21. FOPO's triple 15.6-inch extender adds three screens, which is beyond the two this page covers.

Not recommended

The UPERFECT BE156MF (sold as the Delta until UPERFECT renamed it) is $379.99 at UPERFECT's store on 2026-11-21. That is $50.99 more than Aura's Dual Go Max (379.99 − 329.00). On one cable it gets dimmer: Notebookcheck measured the 2023 UStation Delta at 160 cd/m² on a single USB-C cable, 29% below its 226 cd/m² on the adapter (160 ÷ 226 = 0.71). Notebookcheck also measured very different contrast on its two panels: 471:1 on the upper and 1,026:1 on the lower. Parka Blogs found the screens "cannot achieve maximum brightness" on one cable.
